---
name: edit-in-effectcraft
description: "OSS headless After Effects alternative."
applications:
  - id: effectcraft
    role: primary
---

Pinned release: [v0.7.0](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/releases/tag/v0.7.0).
The standalone CLI installs on demand under `$VOYAGER_HOME/tools/effectcraft/0.7.0`.
macOS: `effectcraft-cli-0.7.0-macos-universal.zip`, extracted with `ditto -x -k`;
binary: `effectcraft-cli-0.7.0-macos-universal/effectcraft-cli`.
Windows: `effectcraft-0.7.0-windows-<arch>-portable.zip` (`effectcraft-cli.exe`).
Linux: `effectcraft-0.7.0-linux-<arch>.tar.gz` (`bin/effectcraft-cli`).
Verify `SHA256SUMS.txt`; macOS additionally supports
`codesign --verify --strict <binary>` and `spctl --assess --type install -vv <binary>`.
The commands below use `effectcraft-cli`.

`commands --json --filter <word>` discovers IDs and parameters.
`script FILE.jsx --empty --save-as FILE.ecproj` runs After Effects-style JavaScript.
`exec <id> --params '<json>' --project FILE` edits a project;
`file.exportLottie` takes `{comp, path}`.
`render --project FILE --comp NAME --out FILE.webm --channels rgba` exports video.
`mcp --empty` serves headless stdio MCP; `--bridge PORT` connects a desktop session.

macOS verification created a composition, exported Lottie and RGBA WebM,
and listed MCP tools. Upstream is alpha: `.aep`/`.aepx` and After Effects
plug-ins are unsupported; render parity is unmeasured. Lottie export reports
unsupported features as warnings.
